identity.title: Audit and freeze the canonical governance surface

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Perform a narrow repository-level audit of overlapping evidence, audit, regression, runtime, and report modules. Document which modules are canonical domain surfaces, services, adapters, compatibility facades, or legacy paths, and add a boundary test only where the current tree can prove an import/coupling invariant.
human_pressure.why_now: The repository already contains parallel-looking modules such as regression.py plus regression/, audit plus audit_package, and multiple evidence layers. Before more features land, ownership must be explicit to prevent semantic duplication.
do_not_misread: Do not perform a broad refactor or move modules for aesthetics.
Do not delete compatibility paths without production evidence.
Do not merge packages simply because names overlap.
red_lines: Audit and freeze ownership; no speculative architecture rewrite.
No public API break without existing contract evidence.

machine_core.goal: Create an evidence-backed canonical-surface map for Ailuros and enforce only proven import/coupling red lines needed to prevent future duplicate semantic ownership.
red_lines: Do not restructure packages unless required by an existing failing boundary invariant.
Do not delete modules solely because names overlap.
Do not introduce a new BLOCKED or HUMAN_REVIEW path.
invariants: Canonical domain models have one documented ownership location.
Adapters may translate but do not own governance semantics.
Compatibility facades are labeled as such rather than silently becoming competing implementations.
Reference-app/runtime-specific concepts remain outside canonical core semantics.

producer.artifact: current repository module tree and boundary docs

consumer.component: future Ailuros implementation packs and reviewers

observable_effect.assertion: A canonical-surface document maps overlapping modules to clear ownership roles and prevents future semantic duplication without broad refactoring.

proofs.assertion: The audit cites actual modules in the current tree, states canonical ownership, and any added boundary test enforces only an existing documented invariant.

failure_semantics: If ownership cannot be proven from current code/docs, mark it unresolved rather than inventing a migration plan.
Potential duplicate modules remain unchanged until separate evidence-backed packs justify consolidation.

steps.title: Inventory overlapping surfaces
details: Inspect evidence, audit/audit_package, regression.py/regression/, core, runtime, projection, signals, reporting, and adapter modules.

steps.title: Assign ownership roles
details: Classify each relevant module as canonical domain model, service, adapter, compatibility facade, presentation/reporting layer, or unresolved.

steps.title: Record red lines
details: Document which layers may depend on which and where governance semantics must not be duplicated.

steps.title: Enforce only proven boundaries
details: If existing test_core_boundary can safely assert a documented invariant, add the smallest test; otherwise keep this documentation-only.

acceptance: A canonical-governance-surface document exists and reflects the actual current tree.
Overlapping-looking modules are classified without speculative deletion/refactor.
Any boundary test enforces only documented existing behavior.

must_check: The audit is grounded in current repository files rather than architectural imagination.
No package move/delete/rename is bundled into the audit.
Canonical ownership and unresolved areas are clearly separated.
reject_if: The pack performs a broad refactor.
Modules are deleted or merged without production evidence.
The audit invents behavior not present in code/docs.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Boundary/doc tests prove the ownership freeze while full suite confirms behavior remains untouched.
